rule: Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings doctrine section coupling
description: `plugin/governance/remediation-doctrine.md` `## Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings` is the single source for how a user's rejection of a finding, and a threat model, persist across review runs. The source pin is the section heading. Five further pins in the same file carry the load-bearing claims. (1) The definition: a user's rejection of a finding and a threat model are decisions, each recorded at its source in the project's durable design records. (2) The key: the recorded decision, never a finding id or a question; rewriting the key back to a finding id or a per-run question turns the suite red. (3) The condition and its obligation in one span: a later finding that contests a recorded decision is a repeat, and the reviewer rejects it by citing the record, lists it for the user before the merge, does not fix it, and never asks again; deleting any one of those four obligations, or the before-the-merge timing, turns the suite red. The span names no surface: where the user sees a repeat, the PR body or a thread reply, is the consumers' text, unpinned here. The same span carries the boundary: a finding that shows a failure the record does not cover is new and gets First-Finding Triage. (4) The write obligation, its condition and its two writers in one span: a user's rejection is recorded before the next review reads it, by the reviewer that asked when the answer reaches it in the same run, the local reviewer in a delivery run and the GitHub reviewer in a PR watch, and otherwise by the next plan as a plan step; deleting the before-the-next-review timing, the same-run reviewer writer or the next-plan fallback turns the suite red. (5) The settled-answer boundary, its condition and its obligation in one span: a settled answer no reviewer asked, a decision the user made before the run or a reply to a planning question, is not a recorded decision, so no reviewer rejects a finding or writes a record on its strength, and a finding that contests it goes to the next plan, which records the decision at its source as a plan step, after which a contesting finding is a repeat. It is load-bearing because a launch decision is free text tied to no question: without this clause a reviewer could treat such an answer as a key, reject an unrelated finding as settled and write a lasting record the user never made, which breaks the single key of pin (2). Rewriting the condition so a settled answer counts as a record, deleting either example, dropping the no-reject or no-record obligation, or routing the contesting finding anywhere but the next plan turns the suite red. The consumers pin the POINTER only, never remedy prose, so honest rewording of the doctrine body does not break them: `plugin/agents/local-reviewer.md`, `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md`, `plugin/agents/overlord.md` and `plugin/agents/cerebrate.md` must still cite the doctrine file with the section name `(Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings)`. What this pin honestly guarantees is exactly that these word sequences exist in these five named files; it claims nothing about meaning. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion that leaves the pinned bytes intact is invisible: surrounding prose that also lets a reviewer ask the user again, or that keys a decision on a finding id elsewhere, stays green; (2) the role-named destination and the branch-or-trunk clause are unpinned, so deleting either alone stays green; (3) whether a finding contests a settled answer stays the reviewer's judgment, which no pin can see, so a reviewer that misreads a contesting finding as unrelated stays green; (4) the pins are whole-file, so moving any pinned sentence out of this section stays green; (5) the pin sees only the five files it names, and no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW reviewer that never points at the section at all, which is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.

consumers.pattern: A user's rejection of a finding and a threat model are decisions, each recorded at its source in the project's durable design records
The key is the recorded decision, never a finding id or a question

A later finding that contests a recorded decision is a repeat: the reviewer rejects it by citing the record, lists it for the user before the merge, does not fix it, and never asks again. A finding that shows a failure the record does not cover is new and gets **First-Finding Triage**

A user's rejection is recorded before the next review reads it: by the reviewer that asked, when the answer reaches it in the same run (the local reviewer in a delivery run, the GitHub reviewer in a PR watch), otherwise by the next plan as a plan step

A settled answer no reviewer asked, such as a decision the user made before the run or a reply to a planning question, is not a recorded decision: no reviewer rejects a finding or writes a record on its strength, and a finding that contests it goes to the next plan, which records the decision at its source as a plan step; from then on, a finding contesting it is a repeat.
